name: Barguna
tagline: Bangladesh's quiet coast — three rivers, the eastern Sundarbans, and beaches the crowds haven't found.

guide.bestTime: November to February (cool, dry, calm sea). Avoid the monsoon and cyclone season, roughly June–October.
guide.gettingThere: By road from Dhaka (~280 km) — much faster since the Padma Bridge opened in 2022, buses ~6–7 hr; also via Barisal (~80 km). Overnight launches run from Dhaka's Sadarghat up the Bishkhali. Nearest airport is Barisal.
guide.difficulty: Moderate — the town and Bibichini are easy, but the best of the coast (Haringhata, Shuvo Sandhya, Sonakata) lies out in Patharghata and Taltali, reached by a mix of bus, motorbike and boat.

mustVisit.name: Haringhata Eco Park & Forest
mustVisit.description: A mangrove forest on the fringe of the Sundarbans in Patharghata, where the Baleshwar, Bishkhali and Payra rivers all empty into the Bay of Bengal — deer, monkeys, birds and a wooden trail through the trees.
mustVisit.history: Part of the coastal mangrove belt continuous with the eastern Sundarbans. A boardwalk and watchtower let visitors walk out over the tidal forest, with the three river mouths meeting the open sea beyond.

practical.hours: Daylight only; go on a falling tide

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 60 km southwest of Barguna town, beyond Patharghata
howToReach.transport: Bus / motorbike to Patharghata, then local transport and a short boat hop

mustVisit.bestTime: Cool months, early morning for wildlife
tips: Wear closed shoes — the mud is sticky
Carry water and a power bank; facilities are minimal
Check tide timings before you set out

mustVisit.name: Shuvo Sandhya Sea Beach
mustVisit.description: A quiet ~4 km beach at Nalbunia in Taltali, at the meeting point of the Payra, Bishkhali and Baleshwar — far less crowded than Kuakata, with a strip of coastal forest behind the sand.
mustVisit.history: An emerging beach destination on Barguna's coast, valued precisely for its emptiness. The shoreline shifts with the rivers and the sea, and casuarina and mangrove line the back of the beach.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 45 km south of Barguna town, in Taltali Upazila
howToReach.transport: Bus / motorbike to Taltali, then local transport to Nalbunia

mustVisit.bestTime: Cool months; sunrise and sunset are both visible along the bend
tips: No lifeguards — swim with great care and mind the currents
Bring your own food; stalls are few

mustVisit.name: Bibichini Shahi Mosque
mustVisit.description: A single-domed Mughal-era mosque from 1659, standing on a 30-foot mound in Betagi — one of the oldest Islamic monuments in the southern coast.
mustVisit.history: Built by Hazrat Shah Neyamat Ullah, who came from Persia to spread Islam, the mosque (33 ft square, with 6-ft-thick walls) is named after his daughter, Bibi Chini. Three graves beside it are said by tradition to hold the saint and his two daughters.

practical.hours: Open during the five daily prayers; visitors welcome outside prayer times

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: In Bibichini Union, Betagi Upazila, north of Barguna town
howToReach.transport: Bus / CNG to Betagi, then easybike to the mound

mustVisit.bestTime: Morning light; outside Friday noon prayers
tips: Cover head if female; remove shoes before entering
Climb the mound for the view over the surrounding fields

mustVisit.name: Sonakata–Asharchar Eco Park (Tengragiri)
mustVisit.description: A sea beach backed by the Tengragiri reserve mangrove forest in Taltali — a wilder, twin attraction to Shuvo Sandhya, with deer in the trees and Rakhine villages nearby.
mustVisit.history: The Sonakata / Asharchar shoreline sits against the Tengragiri (Fatrar-related) reserve forest, a protected mangrove tract on the Barguna coast. The eco park combines beach, forest trails and an aviary-style enclosure.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 50 km south of Barguna town, in Taltali Upazila
howToReach.transport: Bus / motorbike to Taltali, then local transport and boat

mustVisit.bestTime: Cool months; low tide to walk the beach and forest edge
tips: Pair it with a Rakhine para visit, which is close by
Go with a local guide — the forest tracks are easy to lose

mustVisit.name: Patharghata Fishing Harbour
mustVisit.description: One of the country's major marine fish landing centres, where the deep-sea fishing fleet comes in off the Bay — a raw, vivid window into Barguna's fishing economy.
mustVisit.history: Patharghata, at the river mouth on the Bishkhali–Baleshwar, is a hub of Barguna's marine fishing. Trawlers land hilsa and sea fish here, which are sorted, iced and trucked across the country.

practical.hours: Busiest at dawn when the boats unload

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 55 km southwest of Barguna town, at Patharghata

mustVisit.bestTime: Early morning during the fishing season (avoid the annual hilsa-ban months)
tips: Go at first light to see the catch come in
Ask before photographing the fishers and traders

mustVisit.name: Rakhine Para, Taltali
mustVisit.description: The Rakhine community villages of Taltali — Buddhist temples (kyang), traditional handloom weaving, and a culture distinct from the surrounding coast, shared with neighbouring Kuakata.
mustVisit.history: Rakhine families have lived along this coast for generations, keeping their own language, Theravada Buddhist faith and weaving traditions. Their new-year Sangrai festival, with its water-throwing Jalkeli, is the year's high point.

practical.hours: Daytime; respect temple and village schedules

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: In the Taltali coastal belt, ~45 km south of Barguna town
howToReach.transport: Bus / motorbike to Taltali, then local transport

mustVisit.bestTime: Sangrai (Buddhist new year, April) for the water festival
tips: Ask before photographing people and homes
Buy weaving directly from the artisans to support them

specialties.name: Coconut & Coastal Produce
specialties.description: Barguna is one of the country's leading producers of coconut and betel nut — coconut shows up everywhere, from naru and shuruya to everyday cooking.
specialties.venue: Town markets and village haats across the district

specialties.name: Rakhine Handloom Weaving
specialties.description: The Rakhine women of Taltali weave distinctive cotton textiles on traditional looms — bright, sturdy cloth sold from the paras and at Kuakata.

specialties.name: Rakhine Jalkeli (Sangrai Water Festival)
specialties.description: The Rakhine Buddhist new-year festival, where the community welcomes the year by throwing water — dance, music and feasting in the Taltali villages.

specialties.name: Lathi Khela
specialties.description: The Bengali stick-fighting folk martial art, demonstrated by lathials with long bamboo staffs at Pohela Boishakh and harvest gatherings — a living rural tradition in the district.

bucketlist.title: Walk the mangrove boardwalk at Haringhata
bucketlist.detail: A wooden trail leads out over the tidal forest on the Sundarbans fringe — deer, monkeys and birdcall, with the open Bay beyond.

bucketlist.title: Watch three rivers meet the Bay
bucketlist.detail: At Haringhata the Baleshwar, Bishkhali and Payra all pour into the Bay of Bengal — a wide, shifting meeting of fresh and salt water.

bucketlist.title: Have an empty beach to yourself at Shuvo Sandhya
bucketlist.detail: A quiet 4 km beach where the rivers and sea meet — sunrise and sunset both visible, and almost no crowd.

bucketlist.title: Climb to the 1659 Bibichini Shahi Mosque
bucketlist.detail: A single-domed Mughal mosque on a 30-foot mound, built by a Persian saint and named after his daughter Bibi Chini.

bucketlist.title: Explore the Sonakata beach and Tengragiri forest
bucketlist.detail: A wilder beach-and-mangrove combination with deer in the reserve forest and Rakhine villages close by.

bucketlist.title: Visit a Rakhine para and watch the weaving
bucketlist.detail: The Rakhine community keeps its own language, Buddhist temples and handloom weaving along this coast.

bucketlist.title: Join the Rakhine Jalkeli water festival
bucketlist.detail: The Rakhine new-year Sangrai festival welcomes the year by throwing water — dance, music and feasting.

bucketlist.title: Watch the fishing fleet land at Patharghata
bucketlist.detail: At dawn the deep-sea trawlers unload hilsa and sea fish at one of the country's biggest marine landing centres.

bucketlist.title: Eat fresh Bay-of-Bengal hilsa
bucketlist.detail: Hilsa straight off the boats — fried crisp or steamed in mustard, it tastes best this close to where it's caught.

bucketlist.title: Buy Rakhine handwoven cloth
bucketlist.detail: Bright, sturdy cotton woven on traditional looms — buy it directly from the weavers in the paras.

bucketlist.title: Try coconut naru and palm jam
bucketlist.detail: In a district full of coconut and palm, the local sweets and jams are the obvious thing to taste.

bucketlist.title: Catch a Lathi Khela display at Pohela Boishakh
bucketlist.detail: Lathials spin and clash long bamboo staffs in the old Bengali stick-fighting art — a highlight of new-year and harvest gatherings.

foods.name: Bay-of-Bengal Hilsa (Ilish)
foods.description: Fresh hilsa from the Bishkhali, Payra and the sea off Patharghata — fried or in a mustard curry with rice.

foods.name: Marine Fish & Shrimp
foods.description: Sea fish, prawn and shrimp landed by the Patharghata fleet — about as fresh as coastal fish gets.
foods.whereToFind: Patharghata harbour market and local canteens

foods.name: Coconut Naru & Shuruya
foods.description: Coconut sweets — naru (coconut-jaggery balls) and shuruya — from a district awash in coconut.
foods.whereToFind: Town sweet shops and village homes

foods.name: Chui Pitha & Muitta Pitha
foods.description: Regional coastal rice-flour cakes, simple and home-made, especially in winter.

foods.name: Palm Jam (Taal)
foods.description: Jam and sweets made from sugar-palm fruit in the late-summer taal season.

foods.name: Coastal Shutki (Dried Fish)
foods.description: Sun-dried marine fish in the bold southern coastal style — pungent, fiery and cooked into bhuna.

famousPeople.name: Mir Sabbir
famousPeople.knownFor: Popular Bangladeshi television and film actor and director; won the National Film Award for Best Actor for the 2021 film Raat Jaga Phool. Born and raised in Barguna.

famousPeople.name: Mohammed Akhtaruzzaman
famousPeople.knownFor: Historian and academic, a professor and former Vice-Chancellor of the University of Dhaka, from Barguna District.

didYouKnow: Barguna fronts the Bay of Bengal and the eastern Sundarbans — at Haringhata the Baleshwar, Bishkhali and Payra rivers all empty into the sea together.
Bibichini Shahi Mosque was built in 1659 on a 30-foot mound by Hazrat Shah Neyamat Ullah, who came from Persia; the place takes its name from his daughter, Bibi Chini.
Barguna is one of Bangladesh's leading producers of coconut and betel nut.
The Rakhine community of Taltali keeps its own language, Buddhist temples and handloom weaving, and celebrates the new year with the water-throwing Jalkeli festival.
Patharghata is one of the country's major marine fish landing centres, where the deep-sea fishing fleet brings in hilsa and sea fish off the Bay.
